slides.text: Transylvania, Romania. Bran Castle, built in the late 1300s on a rock above a mountain pass.
Every year, crowds of tourists come to see 'Dracula's Castle'.
But Bram Stoker, who wrote Dracula in 1897, never visited Transylvania. His book doesn't mention Bran.
Vlad the Impaler, the real ruler linked to Dracula, never ruled this castle. Most historians say he never set foot inside.
Bran's real story? From 1920, it belonged to Queen Marie of Romania.
Today it's a museum full of her furniture and art.
So why 'Dracula's Castle'? It sits on a cliff like the castle in the novel... and the legend sells tickets.
Dracula never lived here. That doesn't stop people coming to look for him.
